title: The crow and the fox
intro: A crow sits in a tree with a piece of stolen cheese, and a hungry fox below has a plan: a few sweet words. Iranian children learn this old fable at school, usually as a little poem. Read it for flattery and its grammar: comparatives with از همه 'than all', the present perfect ندیده‌ام 'I have never seen', اگر with the subjunctive, and the useful خوشش آمد 'he liked it'.
source: Retold from the ancient fable, known in Iran from school books (public domain).

sentences.fa: یک روز کلاغی از پنجره‌ی خانه‌ای یک تکه پنیر دزدید.
sentences.r: yek ruz kalāgh-i az panjere-ye khāne-i yek tekke panir dozdid.
sentences.en: One day a crow stole a piece of cheese from the window of a house.

sentences.fa: او پرواز کرد و بالای یک درخت بلند نشست.
sentences.r: u parvāz kard o bālā-ye yek derakht-e boland neshast.
sentences.en: It flew off and sat at the top of a tall tree.

sentences.fa: می‌خواست پنیر را با خیال راحت بخورد.
sentences.r: mi-khāst panir rā bā khiyāl-e rāhat bokhorad.
sentences.en: It wanted to eat the cheese in peace.

sentences.fa: روباهی که زیر درخت راه می‌رفت، بوی پنیر را شنید و به بالا نگاه کرد.
sentences.r: rubāh-i ke zir-e derakht rāh mi-raft, bu-ye panir rā shenid o be bālā negāh kard.
sentences.en: A fox that was walking under the tree smelt the cheese and looked up.

sentences.fa: با خودش گفت: «باید آن پنیر را به دست بیاورم.»
sentences.r: bā khod-ash goft: «bāyad ān panir rā be dast biyāvaram.»
sentences.en: It said to itself: "I must get that cheese."

sentences.fa: بعد با صدای شیرین گفت: «سلام، کلاغ زیبا! چه پر‌های سیاه و براقی داری!»
sentences.r: ba'd bā sedā-ye shirin goft: «salām, kalāgh-e zibā! che par-hā-ye siyāh o barrāgh-i dāri!»
sentences.en: Then it said in a sweet voice: "Hello, beautiful crow! What shiny black feathers you have!"

sentences.fa: «من تا حالا پرنده‌ای به این قشنگی ندیده‌ام.»
sentences.r: «man tā hālā parande-i be in ghashangi na-dide-am.»
sentences.en: "I have never seen such a lovely bird."

sentences.fa: «حتماً صدایت هم از همه‌ی پرنده‌ها قشنگ‌تر است.»
sentences.r: «hatman sedā-yat ham az hame-ye parande-hā ghashang-tar ast.»
sentences.en: "Your voice must be the loveliest of all the birds' too."

sentences.fa: «اگر برایم آواز بخوانی، تو را پادشاه پرندگان می‌دانم.»
sentences.r: «agar barā-yam āvāz bekhāni, to rā pādeshāh-e parandegān mi-dānam.»
sentences.en: "If you sing for me, I'll call you the king of the birds."

sentences.fa: کلاغ از این حرف‌ها خیلی خوشش آمد.
sentences.r: kalāgh az in harf-hā kheyli khosh-ash āmad.
sentences.en: The crow liked these words very much.

sentences.fa: او منقارش را باز کرد و با صدای بلند گفت: «قار! قار!»
sentences.r: u menghār-ash rā bāz kard o bā sedā-ye boland goft: «ghār! ghār!»
sentences.en: It opened its beak and cried loudly: "Caw! Caw!"

sentences.fa: همان لحظه پنیر از دهانش افتاد.
sentences.r: hamān lahze panir az dahān-ash oftād.
sentences.en: At that very moment the cheese fell from its mouth.

sentences.fa: روباه آن را در هوا گرفت و فوراً خورد.
sentences.r: rubāh ān rā dar havā gereft o fowran khord.
sentences.en: The fox caught it in mid-air and ate it at once.

sentences.fa: بعد خندید و گفت: «صدایت بد نیست، کلاغ عزیز، اما عقلت کم است!»
sentences.r: ba'd khandid o goft: «sedā-yat bad nist, kalāgh-e aziz, ammā aghl-at kam ast!»
sentences.en: Then it laughed and said: "Your voice isn't bad, dear crow, but you're short of brains!"

sentences.fa: «یادت باشد: به کسی که از تو تعریف می‌کند و چیزی می‌خواهد، زود اعتماد نکن.»
sentences.r: «yād-at bāshad: be kas-i ke az to ta'rif mi-konad o chiz-i mi-khāhad, zud e'temād na-kon.»
sentences.en: "Remember: don't be quick to trust someone who praises you and wants something from you."

sentences.fa: روباه رفت و کلاغ گرسنه روی درخت ماند.
sentences.r: rubāh raft o kalāgh-e gorosne ru-ye derakht mānd.
sentences.en: The fox went away, and the hungry crow was left sitting in the tree.

questions.q: Where did the crow get the cheese?
options: from the window of a house

questions.q: What did the fox praise first?
What did the fox ask the crow to do?

options: the crow opened its beak to sing
don't trust people who flatter you to get something

after: This fable goes back to Aesop and was retold by La Fontaine; Iranian children know it from a little poem in their school reader. Notice how Persian makes a superlative out of a comparative: از همه‌ی پرنده‌ها قشنگ‌تر 'more beautiful than all the birds', i.e. the most beautiful. خوشش آمد 'he liked it' is literally 'it came pleasant to him': the person is the ending on خوش (خوشم آمد 'I liked it', خوشت آمد؟ 'did you like it?'), and the thing liked takes از: از این حرف‌ها خوشش آمد. یادت باشد 'let it be in your memory' means 'remember!'. A Persian crow says قار قار (ghār ghār), and in Iranian tales the crow is a busybody – it is the bird that 'never got home' at the end of every story.
